slides.title: Do school closures close the door to higher education?
slides.body: I linked twenty years of school records with higher-education enrollment, graduation and admission tests to find out.

slides.title: Looking only at the final gap confuses the hospital with the disease
slides.body: Students who lost their high school enter higher education less often (50.61% versus 65.24%, −14.64 points). Yet over four-fifths of that distance (−12.00 points, or 82.0%) already existed in the cohort that studied there four years earlier (G−5).

slides.note: I linked 79,709,054 school enrollment records with 20 SIES Enrollment rosters (2007–2026) and 19 Graduation rosters (2007–2025) using DiD, Double ML and the Orthogonal R-Learner.

slides.kicker: The causal ladder in secondary school (2016–2019)
slides.title: The overall average converges to zero, but the IP/CFT channel contracts
slides.subtitle: Estimated gap in 2-year higher-education entry, secondary school (percentage points).
slides.note: Upper elementary: no detectable drop (+1.21 pp DiD; +1.02 DML). Secondary: university entry (+1.98 pp) and top-20% PAES (+1.75 pp) do not fall; IP/CFT contracts by −2.09 pp (p = 0.0037), with substitution toward universities still open.

slides.kicker: Causal ML heterogeneity (BLP, GATE and CLAN)
slides.unit: in every hundred in the most fragile quintile (G1)
slides.body: In the quintile with the largest predicted harm (G1: 99.5% in secondary school, 77.2% vocational-technical, 87.1% prior attendance), about 12 fewer in every hundred enter higher education when only their individual backpack is controlled for; once the school's prior history is added, that drop is absorbed (−0.26 pp).
slides.note: GATE in G1 with student controls: −12.26 pp in overall entry (−17.79 to −6.74; BLP +0.634, p = 0.0243), −11.48 pp in persistence and −8.02 pp in IP/CFT (p = 0.0007). With G−5 school history, G1 overall entry moves to −0.26 pp, yet IP/CFT heterogeneity persists (BLP +0.425, p = 0.0177).

slides.kicker: Fourteen cohorts (2009–2022) and the clean closure rule
slides.title: Without filtering block transfers, closures get mixed with mergers
slides.subtitle: 2-year higher-education entry rate by episode classification.
slides.note: In secondary, the DiD effect moves from +0.55 pp in 2009–2015 (10,934 exposed) to −2.64 pp in 2016–2019 (−2.59 in IP/CFT) and −3.79 pp in the 2020–2022 pandemic (−4.33 in IP/CFT, −4.72 in persistence); with 7 to 12 high schools per regime, none is distinguishable from zero.

slides.title: What survives the stress tests and what remains open
slides.body: Before drawing policy lessons, I subjected the findings to four boundary and sensitivity checks:
items: Part III debt settled: grade lag (+5.29 pp) withstands 2.54 times the prior trend bound (0.81 pp) and holds at +3.87 pp among G−2 stayers
Cinelli and Hazlett (2020): erasing the −2.09 pp IP/CFT drop requires a hidden confounder over twice as strong as G−5 history (Robustness Value 6.16%; 2.33% at 95%)
Substitution vs. net loss: university entry is +1.98 pp (−0.22 to +4.19); part of the −2.09 pp IP/CFT drop may be diversion, and the individual-trajectory test is still pending
PAES/PDT (2021–2026): with equal history, test-taking (−10.98 pp), enrolling (−7.46) and top 20% (−2.54) cease to differ from zero (+0.75, +2.87 and +1.75 pp)

slides.kicker: So what now for public policy?
slides.title: When a high school closes, relocation does not end with a seat in March
slides.body: The recipe depends on the grade level at closure; these are precautionary safeguards, not estimated effects:
items: Upper elementary (Grades 7 to 8): nearby seats, transport and pedagogical welcome to cushion the immediate grade lag
Secondary school (Grades 9 to 11): named early-warning support for vocational-technical students with low prior attendance (G1 profile)
Vocational-technical articulation: specialty credit recognition and direct guidance into accredited IPs and CFTs
Financial bridge: timely FUAS completion (tuition-free aid and scholarships) and follow-up across the first two postsecondary years
